record.paper_title: Some open problems on the classical function space L1
record.original_question: If X is a subspace of L1[0,1] such that the quotient L1[0,1]/X is isomorphic to c0, must X have the Dunford-Pettis property?

evidence.quote: Problem 12. ([66]) Suppose X is a subspace of L1 with L1/X isomorphic to c0. Does X have the Dunford-Pettis property?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $L^1=L^1[0,1]$ denote the Banach space of (equivalence classes of) Lebesgue-integrable real-valued functions on $[0,1]$, and let $c_0$ denote the Banach space of real sequences converging to $0$, equipped with the supremum norm.

A Banach space $Y$ is said to have the Dunford–Pettis property if for every weakly null sequence $(y_n)$ in $Y$ and every weakly null sequence $(y_n^*)$ in the dual $Y^*$, one has $y_n^*(y_n)\to 0$. Equivalently, every weakly compact operator from $Y$ into any Banach space sends weakly compact sets to norm compact sets.

Suppose $X$ is a closed linear subspace of $L^1[0,1]$ such that the quotient Banach space $L^1[0,1]/X$ is isomorphic to $c_0$. Must $X$ have the Dunford–Pettis property?
artifact.status_search_result: No publication resolving this specific question (whether every subspace X of L^1[0,1] with L^1/X isomorphic to c_0 has the Dunford–Pettis property) was located. It continues to be listed among open problems on L^1, and standard surveys on the Dunford–Pettis property do not record a resolution.

status_evidence.title: Dunford-Pettis property - Encyclopedia of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: Lists known results and open problems on the Dunford–Pettis property; does not record a resolution of this question for subspaces of L^1 with c_0 quotient.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the specific question is recorded in standard references.

status_evidence.title: On the three-space problem for the Dunford-Pettis property
status_evidence.snippet: DPP is not in general a three-space property; subspaces and quotients can have DPP while X does not, and vice versa.
status_evidence.claim: General three-space behavior does not settle the specific L^1/X ≅ c_0 case.
